diagnosis.explanation: Design P088 (Nb2O5/MgF2 Fabry-Perot) shows strong rejection in Visible (G2: 0.183) and NIR (G3: 0.724) bands compared to baseline P009, but suffers from extremely low UV transmission (G1: 2.14e-6). Local derivative analysis indicates that decreasing the cavity thickness (layer_5:dCav) helps G2 but hurts G1 and G3. Increasing the outer mirror layer (layer_8:dH1) is feasible and predicted to help G1 slightly while hurting G2/G3, suggesting a trade-off space exists to recover UV passband transmission without fully sacrificing stopband depth.

Design P027 (6-layer Nb2O5/MgF2 non-quarter-wave stack) demonstrates a different spectral profile with higher UV transmission (G1: 0.0079) than P088, but fails significantly in the NIR band (G3: 0.972). Local derivatives for variables t1, t3, t4, and t5 show that increasing thickness generally helps G2 and G3 (rejection) while hurting G1 (transmission). This confirms the coupling between passband width/height and stopband depth. Refining the shared family variables may find a balance where NIR rejection improves without collapsing the UV signal entirely.

Design P005 (7-layer Fabry-Perot with thick cavity) exhibits moderate UV transmission (G1: 1.64e-4) and good NIR rejection (G3: 0.789), but poor Visible rejection (G2: 0.350). Derivatives indicate that decreasing the high-index layer thickness (dH) or low-index thickness (dL) helps G1 and G2 but hurts G3. Conversely, adjusting the cavity (dCav) offers a trade-off where decreasing it helps G1 and G2 but hurts G3. This suggests the current thick cavity (189nm) might be misaligned for the visible stopband, and refining these three shared variables could sharpen the visible edge.
